levels.name: Level 1 - time and identity
levels.unlocks: Answers questions about any date, and lets an update name what it replaces.

levels.name: Level 2 - provenance and authority
levels.unlocks: Resolves disagreement by rule instead of by guess, and routes a change request to the party accountable for it.

levels.name: Level 3 - disclosure
levels.unlocks: Decides what may cross a boundary without either leaking or over-refusing.

levels.name: Experimental
levels.unlocks: Proposed on the strength of a measured blind spot, not yet tested.

fields.definition: A stable identifier for the record itself, short enough to be written by hand.

evidence.measure: closing the right record on a restatement

fields.definition: The date from which the statement was true. Not the date it was captured.
The date after which it stopped being true. The field must be present; null means it still holds.
Where the statement came from, as an identifier that can be followed.
The single party accountable for what the concept means. One per concept.

evidence.measure: sending a change request to the right owner

fields.definition: The accountable role inside that party, so a request reaches a person.
One rule, stated once per store, for choosing between records that cover the same date and disagree.

evidence.measure: deciding which of two live records stands

fields.requirement: MUST on any record that states a rule
fields.definition: The question classes the rule governs. A rule with no stated scope silently governs more than its author meant.

fields.requirement: MUST on any record that states a rule
fields.definition: The question classes the rule explicitly does not govern. Written separately because a reader cannot infer the negative from the positive.

evidence.measure: internal questions under the same federation rule

fields.requirement: MUST where any record is restricted
fields.definition: The parties permitted to read this record. Absence of the field is not permission.

evidence.measure: releasing what a requester is entitled to

fields.definition: The identifier of the record this one replaces, so an update never has to be expressed by editing history.

A register of the concepts the store is meant to hold, so that a concept missing altogether becomes detectable. Tested once, in a 60-call experiment published beside this profile: the absent concept went from 1 of 3 detections to 3 of 3 with no change in false alarms, but only two of six gaps moved, so the exact sign test over the family is p = 0.5.

evidence.measure: detecting a concept absent from the catalogue

operation.rule: Write one new record. Set its valid_from to the date the new statement begins. Set its supersedes to the record_id it replaces. Do not edit the superseded record and do not compute an end date for it.
operation.derivation: The end of a superseded interval is derived at read time: a record is in force on a date when it covers that date and no record superseding it has a valid_from on or before that date.
operation.rationale: Both benchmarks produced the correct new value on every scenario and the wrong boundary date on a third to a fifth of them. Deriving the boundary removes the step that failed.
operation.incorrect: Editing D-802 to set valid_to, or writing valid_to as 2026-09-30 by hand. Both express the same intent and both are where the measured errors occurred.

superseded.value: customer records are kept for five years after the contract ends

new_record.value: customer records are kept for three years after the contract ends

serialisation.rule: One record per line, fields in the fixed order above, separated by a vertical bar. An empty field means absent; a tilde in valid_to means the interval is open.

selection.rule: Stage one, the agent selects the minimal set of records the question needs. Stage two, the question is answered from that set alone.
selection.measured: In the assembly track of the personal dimension benchmark selection recalled every needed record, chose 1.2 records out of 41, and reduced the supplied context from 10332 to 473 characters with no measurable change in accuracy (p = 0.34).
selection.caution: The reduction is measured; a gain in accuracy is not. Do not claim one.

mappings.name: Bi-temporal knowledge graph
mappings.note: Fact edges carrying valid-at and invalid-at beside the episode they came from. Modelled on the documented shape of Zep and its Graphiti engine.

fields.source: the episodic node the edge was extracted from
fields.concept_owner: add: OWNED_BY edge from the entity to a party node
fields.owner_role: add: role attribute on that OWNED_BY edge
fields.conflict_policy: add: one graph-level property, or a single policy node
fields.applies_to: add: attribute on the rule edge, or SCOPES edges to entity classes
fields.does_not_apply_to: add: EXCLUDES edges from the rule edge
fields.release_to: add: VISIBLE_TO edges, or a list attribute on the fact edge
fields.supersedes: add: SUPERSEDES edge between fact edges
fields.expected_concepts: add: entity nodes marked as expected but unpopulated

mappings.name: Vector memory with timestamps
mappings.note: Extracted memory strings with a write timestamp and filterable metadata. Modelled on the documented shape of a vector-first store such as Mem0.

fields.valid_from: add: metadata field, distinct from the created-at timestamp
fields.conflict_policy: add: one pinned memory, or application configuration
fields.applies_to: add: metadata list on the memory holding the rule
fields.does_not_apply_to: add: metadata list, kept separate from applies_to
fields.release_to: add: metadata list, applied as a retrieval filter
fields.supersedes: add: metadata field holding the prior memory id
fields.expected_concepts: add: a separate register, not a memory

mappings.name: Data catalogue or business glossary
mappings.note: A governed term set beside the store. Modelled on the shape catalogue vendors such as Atlan or Collibra position next to a memory graph.

fields.valid_from: add: usually only the asset has versions, the statement does not
fields.source: lineage link to the source asset
fields.conflict_policy: add: a policy document linked from the glossary
fields.applies_to: policy scope, native in most catalogues
fields.does_not_apply_to: add: catalogues usually state inclusion only
fields.expected_concepts: add: a list of required terms

mappings.name: Wiki or document store
mappings.note: Team pages written by people. Carrying the overlay in the sentence is enough: in the collaborative benchmark a wiki doing exactly this matched the structured representation.

fields.record_id: a short tag written in the line, for example [D-102]
fields.concept_owner: a page listing who owns what
fields.owner_role: the role named on that page
fields.conflict_policy: a page stating how disagreements are settled
fields.applies_to: the sentence says which questions the rule governs
fields.does_not_apply_to: a second sentence saying what it does not govern
fields.release_to: stated in the line that holds the restricted statement
fields.supersedes: the tag of the superseded line, named in the new line

mappings.name: Relational table
mappings.note: One row per statement. The overlay is nine columns and one policy row.

fields.source: foreign key to a source table
fields.concept_owner: foreign key to a party table
fields.conflict_policy: one row in a policy table, referenced by the store
fields.applies_to: join table of rule to question class
fields.does_not_apply_to: the same join table with an excluded flag
fields.release_to: join table of record to party

mappings.name: Vercy Dimension
mappings.note: The native carrier. Present here so the overlay can be read as a subset of it rather than as a separate thing.
